figures.caption: Figure 3: Natural logarithm of the amount of sentences (y-axis) in the BLiMP animacy task for which a proportion of the difference in perplexity is explained by key tokens (x-axis). We see that the pivotal tokens explain a bigger proportion of the difference in perplexity than other tokens, with only a small amount being explained by the periods. However, we can notice as also for this task the pivotal tokens are accountable for only a maximum of ±50% of the difference in perplexity.

Figure 2: Natural logarithm of the amount of sentences (y-axis) in the nonsense words task for which a proportion of the difference in perplexity is explained by key tokens (x-axis). We see that the pivotal tokens explain a bigger proportion of the difference in perplexity then other tokens and/or periods, although only a maximum of ±50% of the difference in perplexity is explained by these tokens.

Figure 6: Natural logarithm of the amount of sentences (y-axis) in the DUST task for which a proportion of the difference in perplexity is explained by key tokens (x-axis). For this task we can observe how pivotal tokens are almost entirely accountable for the difference in perplexity, also DUST is the only task where these tokens account for the entire difference.

Figure 5: Natural logarithm of the amount of sentences (y-axis) in the stereotypes task for which a proportion of the difference in perplexity is explained by key tokens (x-axis). Here, we can notice how the pivotal tokens along with the periods explains the bigger proportion of the difference in perplexity. Again, as for the previous tasks these tokens accounts for only a maximum of ±50% of the difference in perplexity.

Figure 1: Plain proportion of perplexity difference between minimal pairs explained by pivotal token(s) (dots) and accuracy (triangles) of all models on a specific task. Bars represent standard error. Best viewed in color.

Figure 4: Natural logarithm of the amount of sentences (y-axis) in the BLiMP anaphor agreement task for which a proportion of the difference in perplexity is explained by key tokens (x-axis). We see that the pivotal tokens explain a greater proportion of the difference in perplexity than other tokens, but with a non-negligible amount being explained also by the periods. As for the previous task we can notice how the pivotal tokens accounts for only a maximum of ±50% of the difference in perplexity.
